narration.text: In this video, we'll build an interactive dashboard from a file of U.S. flight data, using Claude Code in a GitHub codespace. We won't write any code ourselves.

steps.notes: Episode frame (R30). Motion graphics on screen (R69): text slides over a still of the finished dashboard, rendered in Remotion; see remotion/ OpeningRecap. The take itself starts at p1.01.

narration.text: Claude Code can discover the data, propose options, and build the whole solution. That's powerful, but it's also easy to get a result you didn't want if you don't know how to direct it.

This exercise uses a direction prompt. A direction prompt describes the goal, the audience, and the quality you expect, and leaves the technical decisions to the AI. It's how a manager gives direction to an analyst.

A construction prompt is the opposite. It spells out exactly what to build, such as a bar chart of flights by region, using matplotlib. Use a construction prompt when you know exactly what you want. Use a direction prompt when you know the goal, but not the path.

We'll work through the exercise in order. First, we'll find the data and open Claude Code. Then we'll ask for the dashboard, choose from Claude's options, and let it build. Finally, we'll explore the dashboard, request a fix, and save our work to GitHub.

narration.text: Claude lays out what it found and what it could build. In this run, it offers three layouts and recommends one page of linked charts. Key numbers run across the top, then a map of airports, a trend line and a ranking; a click on one chart filters the others. It also flags things to check, such as cancellation counts that look low, and the 2020 drop in flights, which would dominate any trend. Treat findings like these as things to check, not facts. Another run may suggest different charts, but the shape of the reply is what to expect: findings, options, and questions.

Arrive on its questions ("Questions for you" in the doc's run); read one or two aloud, e.g. cancellations or alert thresholds.
Any data quirks it found on its own (doc's run: missing coordinates, territories): findings to verify, not facts.
